Academy Admissions
Academy Admissions
Welcome to Our Academy We are delighted you are considering joining our academy family! We welcome all children and are committed to creating an inclusive environment where every student can thrive and reach their potential. Whether you are looking for a nursery place, reception entry, or an in-year admission, we are here to support you through the process. Please explore the relevant section below for more information, and feel free to contact us with any questions. We look forward to welcoming your family!
Telephone: 0208 689 7688
Email: info@harrisprimarycroydon.org.uk
Address: Harris Primary Academy Croydon, Thomson Crescent, Croydon, CR0 3JT
Our full policy, with details of our admissions criteria, can be downloaded below. The following information provides a brief summary of the application procedure for Reception and in-year admissions.
Nursery Applications
Please click here to view our Nursery admissions arrangements.
Reception Applications
The Academy has an admission number of 60 in Reception for September 2027.
If your child was born between 1st September 2022 and 31st August 2023 apply by 15th January 2027.
Applications for places in Reception should be made on the home Local Authority’s (LA’s) Common Application Form. These are accessible on the LA’s website and should be submitted in accordance with the LA’s published deadlines for applications (on or before 15 January 2027.)
Open Mornings and Evenings with the Principal
We would love to welcome you to Harris Primary Academy Croydon. Join us for one of our open events to meet our staff, see our classrooms and get a real feel for life at our school. Come and find out why our children love learning here.
Open events for Reception 27/28 are as follows:-

Please complete HPAC Open Events - Reception 27/28 –Fill in form to show your interest. We look forward to meeting you!

In Year Admissions
If you are looking for a place in Harris Primary Academy Croydon because you have recently moved into the area, or your child is at another primary school and you feel that a change of school would benefit their education you are entitled to apply for a school place.
Since September 2013, the law allows you to apply directly to a school or Academy instead of the Local Authority.
You can complete our 'In-year Admission Form' electronically by clicking here.
Please note that there is no guarantee that a place will be available but completing this form will mean you will be offered a place or be added to our waiting list.
If you are interested in joining our academy please email info@harrisprimarycroydon.org.uk to book a one to one tour of the school.
For Parents/Carers who Wish to Appeal
Parent(s) wishing to appeal against the Academy’s decision on admissions, for any year group, should complete an Appeal Form (see below) stating the reason for the appeal, based on the published Admissions Criteria. If you wish to appeal you must contact Admissions at the Academy who will send you an appeals form to complete.
Completed forms should be sent to the Clerk to the Appeal Panel at:
Harris Primary Academy Croydon: Thomson Crescent, Croydon, CR0 3JT
All appeals must be made in writing to Harris Primary Academy Croydon using the appeals form. Appeals for Reception applications for September 2027 must be received by 15th May 2027. All appeals will be heard within 40 school days of the deadline for lodging appeals.
The appeals will be heard, in private, by an Independent appeal Panel. The Clerk to the Appeal Panel will make an appointment within a reasonable time, Appeals may be made in English or the Parents’/Carers’ first language.
· Only one appeal per application is allowed.
· Appeals are conducted in person, and you may bring a friend.
The Appeal Hearing
The Academy will arrange for an Independent Appeals Panel to consider the Academy's reasons for refusal and your reasons for wanting to attend the Academy.
The Panel will consist of 3 people (2 will have education experience and one will be an independent person with no education experience).
The Panel will consider the case put forward by you and the Academy. They must consider the admission arrangements for the Academy and the reasons why you want to attend that particular school. The Panel must exercise its discretion by balancing the weight of your argument (for wanting to attend) against the Academy’s reasons for refusal i.e. the prejudice that one more pupil would cause to the education of the students already offered and the Health and Safety of all the pupils already attending the Academy, also taking into account the Academy's published admission arrangements.
The decision of the Independent Appeals Panel is binding on the admissions authority and the Parents.
Deferred/Delayed Entry
Deferring Your Child’s Start Date
If your child has been offered a place, you can choose to postpone their admission until a later point in the academic year. Your child’s place will remain secure provided they begin attendance no later than the start of the term following their fifth birthday.
Delayed Admission for Summer-Born Pupils
Parents of summer-born children (those with birthdays falling between April 1st and August 31st) may apply for their child to join Reception one year later than usual. This means your child would commence Reception in the September after turning five, rather than the September after turning four.
To make this request and for further guidance, it is recommended to contact the Croydon Council Admissions Team https://www.croydon.gov.uk/schools-and-education/schools/school-admissions/admission-children-outside-their-normal-year-group
If you have any questions regarding admissions, please contact our school office

Wrap Around Care
Breakfast and After School Club
At Harris Primary Academy Croydon, we offer Breakfast Club and After School Club provision for all children from Reception to Year 6 whose families need this service. Both clubs are well-structured, engaging and enjoyable.
We aim to provide every child in our care with a safe, nurturing and stimulating environment beyond the normal school day. Our Breakfast Club and After School Club operate through a collaborative approach, working in partnership with families to deliver the highest quality care for all children. We welcome open and confidential discussions about any matters.
To book a place, please contact the academy office for a link to an application form. Parents are billed half termly or montlhy and payments must be made in advance using ParentPay. We are able to support parents using Childcare Tax vouchers or who may need to pay monthly if they are in receipt of Universal Credit. If either of these apply to you, please speak to a member of the office staff.
7.30am – start of school day
Cereal, toast etc. provided
End of school day – 6.00pm
Hot dinner provided (see sample menu in document below)
Where we are oversubscribed for spaces, places will be offered in the following criteria:
1) Looked after/previously looked after children 2) Children with exceptional medical/social need 3) Children of staff members 4) First come first served on completing the online booking form
To apply for a place in our wrap around provision, please click here. Please note that your place is not confirmed until a member of the office team have been in contact.
Out of Hours Contact If you need to contact us about wraparound care outside of school office hours. please call: 07990 004 214 This number is available from 4:30pm until 6pm (Monday-Friday)

Our Ethos
Our Ethos
Whatever a child’s background or starting point, we want to make sure that they leave us with the academic knowledge and social skills necessary to succeed.
As a Harris Federation primary, we believe that everybody has the right to feel safe, happy and respected. The whole community strive for Harris Primary Academy Croydon to be best it can possibly be which is encapsulated by our vision statement: “Excellence: every child, every day”. Our core values of: Perseverance, Achievement and Kindness, underpin everything that happens in our academy and we have high expectations that these are followed and modelled by all staff, parents and children.
As a result of the exceptional practice at our school every single day our children achieve outstanding outcomes each year and we are incredibly proud of them. Alongside academic achievement, we want our academy to be a safe and caring space with the children excited and happy to come to school every day to learn, grow and develop.
All children are treated fairly and we acknowledge individual needs. We expect all our children to work to the best of their abilities and to allow others to do the same. Our 'Golden Rules' underpin our academy ethos:
Show Respect
Take Responsibility
Always Make the Right Choice
HPAC Community Champions
Our Community Champion themes are revisited each year, to ensure children leave HPAC with a clear understanding of these topics and a commitment to being champions of these areas themselves in their future lives. We feel passionate that these themes should not only be taught discretely and instead should form the foundation, rather than an ‘add on’ or tokenistic teaching approach. Although a monthly theme has been chosen, this does not mean to say these topics are not covered throughout the year, rather that we believe it is important to explore the theme in greater detail discreetly. Furthermore, we intend to add other key advocates to the overview in the document below and welcome any suggestions. We are looking forward to working with our parents and local community to support us with our challenges and events. For more information, please see the documents below.

In Year Admissions
If you are looking for a place in Harris Primary Academy Croydon because you have recently moved into the area, or your child is at another primary school and you feel that a change of school would benefit their education you are entitled to apply for a school place.
Since September 2013, the law allows you to apply directly to a school or Academy instead of the Local Authority.
You can complete our 'In-year Admission Form' electronically by clicking here.
Please note that there is no guarantee that a place will be available but completing this form will mean you will be offered a place or be added to our waiting list.
If you are interested in joining our academy please email info@harrisprimarycroydon.org.uk to book a one to one tour of the school.
For Parents/Carers who Wish to Appeal
Parent(s) wishing to appeal against the Academy’s decision on admissions, for any year group, should complete an Appeal Form (see below) stating the reason for the appeal, based on the published Admissions Criteria. If you wish to appeal you must contact Admissions at the Academy who will send you an appeals form to complete.
Completed forms should be sent to the Clerk to the Appeal Panel at:
Harris Primary Academy Croydon: Thomson Crescent, Croydon, CR0 3JT
All appeals must be made in writing to Harris Primary Academy Croydon using the appeals form. Appeals for Reception applications for September 2027 must be received by 15th May 2027. All appeals will be heard within 40 school days of the deadline for lodging appeals.
The appeals will be heard, in private, by an Independent appeal Panel. The Clerk to the Appeal Panel will make an appointment within a reasonable time, Appeals may be made in English or the Parents’/Carers’ first language.
· Only one appeal per application is allowed.
· Appeals are conducted in person, and you may bring a friend.
The Appeal Hearing
The Academy will arrange for an Independent Appeals Panel to consider the Academy's reasons for refusal and your reasons for wanting to attend the Academy.
The Panel will consist of 3 people (2 will have education experience and one will be an independent person with no education experience).
The Panel will consider the case put forward by you and the Academy. They must consider the admission arrangements for the Academy and the reasons why you want to attend that particular school. The Panel must exercise its discretion by balancing the weight of your argument (for wanting to attend) against the Academy’s reasons for refusal i.e. the prejudice that one more pupil would cause to the education of the students already offered and the Health and Safety of all the pupils already attending the Academy, also taking into account the Academy's published admission arrangements.
The decision of the Independent Appeals Panel is binding on the admissions authority and the Parents.
Deferred/Delayed Entry
Deferring Your Child’s Start Date
If your child has been offered a place, you can choose to postpone their admission until a later point in the academic year. Your child’s place will remain secure provided they begin attendance no later than the start of the term following their fifth birthday.
Delayed Admission for Summer-Born Pupils
Parents of summer-born children (those with birthdays falling between April 1st and August 31st) may apply for their child to join Reception one year later than usual. This means your child would commence Reception in the September after turning five, rather than the September after turning four.
To make this request and for further guidance, it is recommended to contact the Croydon Council Admissions Team https://www.croydon.gov.uk/schools-and-education/schools/school-admissions/admission-children-outside-their-normal-year-group
If you have any questions regarding admissions, please contact our school office

Nursery
The Nursery at Harris Primary Academy Croydon is an Early Years provision with warm and welcoming staff. Our staff are a dedicated team of individuals who work together in a professional manner to promote a wide and varied Early Years Provision.
Our highly qualified and experienced staff offer the children learning through play based experiences, under the areas of the Early Years Foundation Stage Curriculum. This contributes to the development of the ‘whole child’ as our aim is to enable all our children to have fun and foster a love for learning. We welcome your involvement in your child’s learning and development and hold regular open mornings so you can be involved in your child's learning and talk to staff.
At Harris Primary Croydon, we are proud of the unique provision we are able to offer our families. At present, all three and four year olds are entitled to 15 hours of free childcare per week, up to 38 weeks per year. The government has also introduced an extended 15 hours of free childcare per week - 30 hours in total for 38 weeks per year, for those families that are eligible.
We can assist you with the eligibility criteria for the universal 15 hours free child care and extended 15 hours free child care (30 hours).
Information about the extended 30 hours free childcare can also be found by visiting the following website:
https://www.gov.uk/30-hours-free-childcare
Parents/carers have the option to use either their entitled 15 or 30 hours of free child care or pay for additional provision.
15-hour government funding:
Morning session: 8.40am - 11.40am, or afternoon session: 12.20pm - 3.20pm.
30-hour government funding-including a FREE hot lunch:
Full Day: 8.40am – 2.40pm
Extended nursery day to 8:40am - 3:20pm- including a FREE hot lunch:
There is an option to extend the nursery day to 3.20pm for an additional fee which will be £6.00 per day.

Why should you choose our Nursery?
Our Nursery Class
The Nursery at Harris Primary Academy Croydon is an Early Years provision with warm and welcoming staff, that are a dedicated team of individuals working together to promote high-quality Early Years provision.
Our highly qualified and experienced staff offer the children a learning through play-based experience as required for the Early Years Foundation Stage Curriculum.
Our Nursery offers 52 places (26 each session). Children can start in Nursery the term after their third birthday, if places are available.
Our Nursery will run term time only in line with the term dates for the main school.
A child may start at the Nursery at different points in the academic year, based on the date of their 3rd birthday.
Applications received after this date will be treated as late applications, and will not be processed until after all on-time applications have been processed, reducing the child's chances of achieving a place.
Nursery Admissions: How to Apply
We are delighted that you are considering a place at our Nursery. Please read the following information carefully to ensure your application is submitted correctly and on time.
1. Complete the Nursery Application Form To apply, at least one parent must complete the Nursery Application Form. This form is available:
Please note: There is no preference given to online or paper submissions. All applications are treated equally.
2. Check the Application Opening Date It is essential that you submit your application form from the correct date and time. Please note, your child becomes eligible for a nursery space, the term following your child’s third birthday. Please refer to the table in Section 6.2 of our Nursery Entry Policy or below, to determine when you can apply. Please note: Applications submitted before the opening date will not be accepted.
3. Submit Your Application Once completed, you can submit the form (from 10am on the respective day):
4. 30 Hours Funding If you are applying for a full-time place using the government’s 30 hours funding, please include your funding code on the application form.
5. Notification of Outcome You will receive a written response within 10 school days of submitting your application.
6. Applying Between Terms
If your child is eligible and you are applying between official application periods, please feel free to contact the Academy directly. There may be places available, and we will be happy to advise you on current availability and next steps.
If you have any questions, please contact the academy office – we are happy to help.

Free School Meals
Free School Meals
Free School Meals / Pupil Premium Payments are available to all eligible pupils attending Croydon maintained schools.
Since September 2014 primary pupils in Reception, Year 1 and Year 2 have received free school meals automatically but it is still necessary for parents of these pupils, who receive one or more of the qualifying benefits listed below, to complete a Free School Meal/Pupil Payment Premium application in order for the child's school to benefit from the additional Pupil Premium funding.
For pupils in all other year groups an application must be submitted to secure both Free School Meals and the Pupil Premium Payment.
In September 2023 - July 2024, children in Years 3 - 6 are also entitled to receive a free lunch every day.
Who should apply?
Parents of children aged four or over attending a maintained school in Bromley who receive child benefit for the child/children and one or more of the following:
Income Support (IS)
Income Based Jobseekers Allowance (IBJSA)
Income-related employment and support allowance (IRESA)
Guaranteed Element of State Pension Credit
How to apply;
Apply for free school meals online at Croydon.gov.uk or by contacting the academy office, who will be happy to help.

Welcome from the Head of Academy
Welcome from the Head of Academy
Our aim for pupils at Harris Primary Academy Croydon (HPAC) is for them to develop into happy, confident and independent individuals who are motivated by a real love of learning.
We have high expectations for every child and provide expert teaching so that our pupils make excellent progress. We place a strong emphasis on the dedicated teaching of reading, writing and maths so that our pupils have a solid foundation to build their learning in other subjects. Our curriculum is rich, varied and engaging and develops children's knowledge, understanding and skills in all subjects. We have high hopes for every pupil, regardless of their background or starting point.
Every day our pupils, teachers and staff all contribute to making our academy a warm and welcoming place to learn. I am very proud of our pupils' positivity towards their learning and the kindness they display towards their teachers and each other.
We are very much a community school and, as well as developing local links and partnerships, we encourage our pupils to be polite, caring and outstanding members of their local community. This, we hope, will help enable our pupils to become compassionate, ambitious, global citizens of the future. We also know that a close partnership with parents and carers is vital and we do all we can to keep them informed and involved in all aspects of school life.
Harris Primary Academy Croydon joined the Harris Federation in 2020 and is part of a family of primary, secondary and all-through academies in and around London. We have many successful Harris academies nearby in the borough and, as part of a thriving community of schools, we benefit from the ability to share, learn, support and challenge each other.
We hope that this website provides a helpful introduction to our academy and while it cannot show you everything, we hope it inspires you to find out more.
If you have any questions about our academy, or if you would like to arrange a tour, please do not hesitate to get in touch.
Zainab Ladak
